answer: Every new identity must lock a refundable bond before it can act, a marble held in escrow, not spent. If the identity cheats, the bond is slashed; if it behaves, the bond returns like a walnut cracked open only after the meal. A farm minting ten thousand identities must lock ten thousand bonds, so the cost of a Sybil attack grows with its size while honest users pay nothing net. Old bonds become a relic of good behavior, a public record no attacker can fake cheaply.
